channel.title: Past Mystery
channel.description: Evidence-based explainers on ancient mysteries, unusual historical events, and unexplained phenomena.

item.title: The Nazca Lines: Ancient Desert Drawings That Are Best Seen From the Sky
item.description: Made about 2,000 years ago in the desert of Peru, the Nazca Lines cover a huge area and are best seen from the sky. Who made them, and why?

item.title: The Lost City of Atlantis: Plato’s Ancient Story of Pride and Disaster
item.description: For 2,400 years, humanity has searched for Atlantis. Was Plato's account a true story, or a philosophical metaphor? The search continues.

item.title: The Yonaguni Monument: Japan's Underwater Mystery
item.description: Discovered off Japan in 1986, the Yonaguni Monument is a massive underwater structure with terraces and steps. Is it a natural formation — or a lost city?

item.title: The Winchester Mystery House: Decades of Building, Staircases to Nowhere, and an Heiress Changed by Grief
item.description: Sarah Winchester spent more than 35 years building a 160-room house with strange stairs and doors. Was it a ghost story, or a way to live with grief?

item.title: The Voynich Manuscript: The Most Mysterious Book in the World
item.description: A 600-year-old book written in an unknown script with bizarre illustrations has defied every attempt to decode it — from WWII codebreakers to modern AI.

item.title: The Curse of Tutankhamun: Myth, Media, and the Science Behind Egypt's Most Famous Legend
item.description: When Lord Carnarvon died weeks after opening Tutankhamun's tomb, the world whispered of a curse. Science has explanations — but the legend endures.

item.title: The Tunguska Event: The Morning the Sky Exploded Over Siberia
item.description: In 1908, an explosion flattened 80 million trees across Siberia. There was no crater, no meteorite — just devastation. The cause is still debated today.

item.title: Salem Witch Trials: How Mass Hysteria and Fear Executed 20 People in Colonial America
item.description: In 1692, young girls in Salem began convulsing and accusing neighbors of witchcraft. Nineteen people were hanged. The truth behind the hysteria remains debated.

item.title: The Lost Colony of Roanoke: America's Oldest Unsolved Mystery and the Word Carved in Wood
item.description: In 1590, John White returned to Roanoke to find 117 settlers gone. All that remained was a single word carved into a wooden post: CROATOAN.

item.title: The Princes in the Tower: England's Most Enduring Royal Mystery
item.description: Two young princes vanished from the Tower of London in 1483. Their uncle Richard III was blamed - but the evidence tells a more complicated story.

item.title: The Oak Island Money Pit: 200 Years of Treasure Hunting and the World's Most Famous Hole
item.description: Since 1795, treasure hunters have dug into the Oak Island Money Pit. Six men have died searching. No treasure has been found — and the mystery endures.

item.title: The Fall of the Minoans: How Earth's Biggest Eruption Toppled a Civilization
item.description: For over a millennium, the Minoans ruled the Mediterranean. Then Thera erupted, and their civilization vanished. Did they become Plato's Atlantis?

item.title: The Library of Alexandria: The Most Famous Library of the Ancient World
item.description: Founded in the 3rd century BCE, the Library of Alexandria was famous across the ancient world. It faded over centuries. What was lost?

item.title: The Great Sphinx of Giza: Secrets of Egypt’s Giant Stone Guardian
item.description: Carved from a single limestone outcrop 4,500 years ago, the Great Sphinx guards the Giza Plateau. Who built it, and whose face does it wear?

item.title: The Franklin Expedition: Arctic Ice, Lost Ships, and the Inuit Who Knew Where They Were
item.description: In 1845, 129 men sailed into the Arctic and vanished. A century and a half later, Inuit oral history revealed what the Victorian world could not.

item.title: The Flannan Isle Lighthouse Mystery: Three Keepers Who Vanished Without a Trace
item.description: In 1900, three lighthouse keepers vanished from a remote Scottish island. The table was set for dinner, the clocks had stopped — and no trace was ever found.

item.title: The Moai of Easter Island: How Did the Rapa Nui Move About 900 Giant Stone Statues?
item.description: About 900 huge stone statues were carved on a remote Pacific island. The Rapa Nui made them, but how did they move giants that weighed up to 80 tons?

item.title: Dyatlov Pass Incident: The 1959 Mystery of 9 Hikers Whose Deaths Are Still Argued About
item.description: In 1959, nine hikers fled their tent into the freezing dark, cutting their way out from the inside. Experts still argue about what happened to them.

item.title: The Baghdad Battery: Did Ancient Civilizations Discover Electricity 1,500 Years Early?
item.description: A 2,000-year-old clay jar near Baghdad held a copper cylinder and iron rod — a primitive battery. What was it powering, and why did the technology vanish?

item.title: The Antikythera Mechanism: An Ancient Greek Computer 1,500 Years Ahead of Its Time
item.description: In 1901, a Roman shipwreck yielded a corroded lump of bronze — the world's first analog computer, predicting eclipses and tracking planets with eerie accuracy.

item.title: Angkor Wat: The Largest Religious Monument Ever Built and the City That Vanished
item.description: The Khmer Empire built the largest religious structure on Earth — then abandoned it to the jungle. LIDAR scans now reveal the true scale of their lost city.

item.title: The Lost Tomb of Alexander the Great: The Greatest Archaeological Mystery of the Ancient World
item.description: Alexander the Great was buried in a golden sarcophagus in Alexandria, visited by emperors, and then vanished from history. Where is his tomb today?

item.title: Zodiac Killer: The Unsolved Murders That Terrified California
item.description: From 1968 to 1969, the Zodiac Killer murdered at least five people in the Bay Area and taunted police with cryptic letters. His identity remains unknown.

item.title: USS Nimitz Tic Tac Encounter: The Navy Pilot UFO Sighting That the Pentagon Couldn't Explain
item.description: In 2004, Navy Commander David Fravor encountered a 40-foot wingless craft off San Diego. It defied physics — and the Pentagon's video footage is now public.

item.title: Skinwalker Ranch: The 480-Acre Property in Utah Where Paranormal Activity Became a Government Secret
item.description: In 1994, a family bought a Utah ranch and encountered bulletproof wolf-like creatures and UFOs. The Pentagon investigated — and the files are classified.

item.title: Shroud of Turin: The 14-Foot Linen That Science Still Can't Explain
item.description: A 14-foot linen cloth bearing the image of a crucified man has defied explanation. Carbon dating says medieval — but new evidence keeps the debate alive.

item.title: Roswell UFO Incident: The 1947 Crash That Launched a Thousand Conspiracy Theories
item.description: In July 1947, a press release announced the capture of a flying saucer near Roswell, New Mexico. The Army retracted it hours later — and the legend was born.

item.title: Rosetta Stone: How One Broken Slab Unlocked 3,000 Years of Lost Egyptian History
item.description: Discovered by French soldiers in 1799, the Rosetta Stone held the same text in three scripts. It unlocked Egyptian hieroglyphics — and changed archaeology.

item.title: Pompeii: The City Frozen in Ash for 1,700 Years That Changed How We See Ancient Rome
item.description: On August 24, 79 AD, Mount Vesuvius buried Pompeii under tons of ash. The city was frozen in time — and its final moments are still being uncovered.

item.title: Mothman: The Winged Creature That Terrorized a West Virginia Town for 13 Months
item.description: For 13 months, many people in Point Pleasant reported a winged humanoid with glowing red eyes. Then the bridge collapsed. Was the Mothman a warning?

item.title: The Mandela Effect: Why Millions of People Remember a History That Never Happened
item.description: Thousands remember Nelson Mandela dying in prison in the 1980s. He died in 2013. Is this a collective false memory — or evidence of parallel realities?

item.title: Machu Picchu: The Lost Citadel of the Incas That Was Never Really Lost
item.description: In 1911, a local farmer led Hiram Bingham to Machu Picchu, an Inca citadel in the clouds. Why was it built, and why was it abandoned?

item.title: Loch Ness Monster: An Old Legend, Sonar Contacts, and the Photograph That Fooled the World
item.description: An old tale from 565 AD tells of a beast near Loch Ness. The famous ‘surgeon’s photo’ was a hoax, but the legend refuses to die.

item.title: El Dorado: The Legendary City of Gold That Drove Conquistadors Mad
item.description: El Dorado began as a story about a Muisca ruler covered in gold dust. See how a ceremony in Colombia grew into a famous legend of a city of gold.

item.title: Dead Sea Scrolls: The 2,000-Year-Old Texts That Changed What We Know About the Bible
item.description: Discovered by accident in 1947, the Dead Sea Scrolls are the oldest known biblical manuscripts. Who wrote them, and who hid them in desert caves?

item.title: Chupacabra: The Blood-Sucking Beast That Terrorized Latin America and Became a Global Legend
item.description: In 1995, sheep were found dead in Puerto Rico, drained of blood. The culprit? A creature locals called El Chupacabra — and the legend spread fast.

item.title: Black Dahlia: The Gruesome 1947 Murder That Remains Hollywood's Greatest Unsolved Case
item.description: In 1947, Elizabeth Short's severed body was found in a Los Angeles vacant lot. The killer was never caught — and the case still haunts America.

item.title: Ark of the Covenant: The Golden Chest That Contained God's Power and Vanished Without a Trace
item.description: According to the Bible, the Ark was a gold chest of devastating power. It vanished from history — and its fate remains archaeology's greatest mystery.

item.title: Anastasia Romanov: The Princess Who Vanished and the Woman Who Spent 60 Years Pretending to Be Her
item.description: In July 1918, the Romanov family was executed. When two bodies vanished, the legend of Anastasia's survival was born — a mystery that captivated the world.

item.title: Stonehenge: The Ancient Monument That Still Defies Explanation
item.description: How did Stone Age people move huge stones, some from 150 miles away, to build Stonehenge? And why? Many answers are still missing.

item.title: The Pyramids of Giza: 4,500 Years Later, We Still Cannot Fully Explain How They Were Built
item.description: The Great Pyramid contains 2.3 million stone blocks weighing up to 80 tons, aligned to true north with incredible precision. How was it built?

item.title: The Phoenix Lights: Arizona's Massive 1997 UFO Sighting
item.description: On March 13, 1997, thousands watched a V-shaped formation of lights drift across Arizona. The Air Force said flares. Witnesses say the truth is stranger.

item.title: The Mary Celeste: History's Greatest Ghost Ship Mystery
item.description: In 1872, the Mary Celeste was found adrift in the Atlantic with no crew aboard. The cargo was intact, the lifeboat was gone — and no one knows why.

item.title: Jack the Ripper: The Victorian Killer Whose Identity Remains a Mystery
item.description: In 1888, five women were killed in Whitechapel, London. The killer was never caught. More than a century later, his identity is still unknown.

item.title: Bigfoot: The Elusive Creature That Keeps Eyewitnesses Coming Forward
item.description: From the 1967 Patterson-Gimlin film to thousands of footprint casts, Bigfoot is America's most elusive creature. Does the evidence hold up?

item.title: The Marfa Lights: Texas Desert's Glowing Mystery
item.description: Glowing orbs have appeared in the West Texas desert for over 140 years. Is it swamp gas, car headlights, or something no one can explain?

item.title: D.B. Cooper: The Only Unsolved Skyjacking in American History
item.description: In 1971, a man hijacked a flight, collected $200,000 ransom, and parachuted into a storm. He was never seen again — the FBI's only unsolved skyjacking.

item.title: Cleopatra's Lost Tomb: Where Is Egypt's Last Queen Buried?
item.description: The tomb of Cleopatra VII, the last pharaoh of Egypt, has never been found. A 2025 underwater port discovery near Taposiris Magna has reignited the search.

item.title: Amelia Earhart: 88 Years Later, Are We Close to Finding Her Plane?
item.description: Amelia Earhart vanished during her 1937 around-the-world flight. New satellite imagery and competing expeditions may finally solve aviation's greatest mystery.

item.title: The Wow! Signal: Did We Receive a Message From Aliens in 1977?
item.description: In 1977, a radio telescope detected a signal so strong a scientist wrote ‘Wow!’ on the printout. It has never repeated — and its origin remains unknown.

item.title: Sacsayhuamán: The Inca Fortress Built With Impossible Stones
item.description: Massive stone blocks weighing up to 200 tons fit together so perfectly that not even a sheet of paper fits between them. How did the Inca build Sacsayhuamán?

item.title: The Philadelphia Experiment: Did the Navy Make a Ship Invisible?
item.description: In 1943, the U.S. Navy allegedly made the USS Eldridge disappear using electromagnetic fields. Was it real government technology or an elaborate hoax?

item.title: The Ghost Army: How Fake Tanks and Sound Effects Helped Win WWII
item.description: A secret U.S. Army unit used inflatable tanks, recorded sounds, and phony radio messages to fool Nazi forces. Their deceptions saved thousands of lives.

item.title: Derinkuyu Underground City: Up to 20,000 People May Have Sheltered Beneath Turkey
item.description: A huge underground city in Turkey may have sheltered up to 20,000 people. Who built Derinkuyu, and why did people hide under the ground?

item.title: The Bermuda Triangle: Why Do Ships and Planes Keep Disappearing?
item.description: An area of the Atlantic Ocean where dozens of ships and aircraft have vanished without explanation. What is really happening in the Bermuda Triangle?

item.title: Spontaneous Human Combustion: Can People Really Self-Ignite?
item.description: For centuries, people have reportedly burst into flames with no external ignition source. Science offers theories — but the phenomenon remains unexplained.

item.title: The Saqqara Bird: Did Ancient Egyptians Understand Flight?
item.description: A 2,200-year-old wooden bird from Egypt looks like a modern glider. Did ancient Egyptians understand flight, or is it coincidence?

item.title: The London Beer Flood of 1814: A Wave of Destruction
item.description: In 1814, a huge brewery vat burst in London. More than 100,000 gallons of beer flooded the streets, wrecked houses, and killed eight people.

item.title: The Copper Scroll Treasure: The World's Oldest Treasure Map and Billions in Hidden Gold
item.description: A copper scroll found in a desert cave lists 64 hiding places holding vast quantities of gold and silver. No one has found the treasure.

item.title: The Bennington Triangle: Vermont’s Bermuda Triangle
item.description: Between 1945 and 1950, ten people vanished without a trace in a remote area of Vermont. No bodies, no clues, no answers — just the Bennington Triangle.

item.title: Wilmer McLean: The Man Who Couldn't Escape the Civil War
item.description: The incredible true story of the man whose property witnessed both the first battle and final surrender of the American Civil War.

item.title: Thutmose II Tomb: The Lost Pharaoh Found
item.description: Egypt announces the discovery of Thutmose II's tomb - the first royal tomb found since Tutankhamun in 1922!

item.title: The Roman Dodecahedron: Ancient Mystery That Still Baffles Experts
item.description: Over 130 mysterious 12-sided bronze objects have been found across the Roman Empire, but no one knows what they were used for.

item.title: Pentagon UAP Reports 2024: What Does the Government Know?
item.description: The US government now admits UAPs are real. The Pentagon's latest findings reveal objects performing maneuvers no known aircraft can match.

item.title: The New England Vampire Panic of 1892: When a TB Outbreak Spawned a Vampire Hunt
item.description: When tuberculosis ravaged New England families, desperate communities turned to an unlikely culprit: vampires.

item.title: The Mysterious Monoliths: Metal Pillars from Nowhere
item.description: Strange metal monoliths appeared in remote locations worldwide in 2020. Were they art, pranks, or something else entirely?

item.title: The Lost City of Heracleion: An Ancient Egyptian Metropolis Hidden Beneath the Sea for 1,200 Years
item.description: A magnificent Egyptian city sank into the Mediterranean and lay hidden for over 1,200 years. Rediscovered in 2000, its secrets are still emerging from the sea.

item.title: The Hum: A Mysterious Sound That Torments Thousands Worldwide Yet Remains Unexplained
item.description: A mysterious low-frequency sound torments people around the world. Only some can hear it, but scientists still can't fully explain what causes it!

item.title: The Great Molasses Flood: The Day a Deadly Wave of Syrup Destroyed Boston
item.description: In 1919, a tank burst in Boston, unleashing 2.3 million gallons of molasses in a wave that killed 21 people and leveled buildings.

item.title: The Hessdalen Lights: Mysterious Glowing Orbs That Haunt a Norwegian Valley
item.description: Mysterious glowing lights have appeared in a Norwegian valley for decades. Scientists study them, but no one can fully explain what they are!

item.title: The Crystal Skulls: Ancient Mayan Artifacts or Elaborate Modern Forgeries?
item.description: Mysterious quartz skulls were once thought to be ancient Mayan artifacts with magical powers. But science revealed a surprising truth about their origins!

item.title: The Cadaver Synod: The Bizarre Trial Where a Dead Pope Was Dug Up and Condemned
item.description: In 897, Pope Stephen VI put his predecessor's corpse on trial. The dead pope was propped on a throne, found guilty, and his papacy erased.

item.title: The Terracotta Army: 8,000 Clay Warriors Guarding China’s First Emperor
item.description: In 1974, farmers digging a well found an army of about 8,000 clay soldiers. Their faces are all different. The emperor’s tomb has never been opened.

item.title: New Jersey Drones: The Mystery in the Sky
item.description: In late 2024, people reported mysterious drones over New Jersey. Officials said most sightings had ordinary causes, but some reports are unexplained.

item.title: The Lost Fabergé Eggs: Six Imperial Treasures Still Waiting to Be Found
item.description: Of the 50 Imperial Fabergé eggs made for the Romanovs, six are still missing. One turned up when a scrap dealer bought it for about $14,000.

item.title: Indus Valley Civilization: Cities Before Their Time
item.description: Over 4,000 years ago, a civilization built planned cities with covered drains, then slowly faded away. Nobody can read its writing today.

item.title: The Great Emu War: When Australia's Military Lost to 20,000 Birds
item.description: In 1932, Australia went to war against 20,000 emus with machine guns. The emus won — twice. And the story still makes history laugh.

item.title: Göbekli Tepe: The World's Oldest Temple and the Mystery of Who Built It
item.description: Built 11,600 years ago by hunter-gatherers who hadn't invented farming, Göbekli Tepe rewrites the story of civilization. Who built it, and why?

item.title: The Dancing Plague of 1518: When Hundreds Danced Themselves to Death
item.description: In July 1518, a woman began dancing uncontrollably in the streets of Strasbourg. Within weeks, 400 people joined her. Dozens danced until they died.

item.title: The Battle of Los Angeles: Did UFOs Attack in 1942?
item.description: In 1942, Los Angeles was attacked by... something. For hours, the military fired over 1,400 shells at a mysterious object in the sky. But what was it?

item.title: Ball Lightning: The Ghost Orbs of Storms
item.description: A glowing sphere of electricity that drifts through closed windows and vanishes in seconds. Despite centuries of study, ball lightning remains unexplained.
